THE PROGRAM (mission register INFRASTRUCTURE.GRAPH frontier, 07-28: 'DECIDED is not the bottleneck, ADOPTION is' -- 92% of the scheduled estate sits on UTC-only Rules while the timezone-aware Scheduler standard exists): (P1) freshness discipline -- trigger-map re-emitted on estate change, drift gate stays green; (P2) DST-RISK RANKING -- classify every enabled Rule as market-anchored (a UTC cron that must track Eastern; silently drifts an hour at DST) vs UTC-anchored-by-design (chain-relative, correct as-is); market-anchored is the migration queue, UTC-anchored is NOT migrated for uniformity's sake; (P3) the migration waves -- Rules -> Scheduler with ScheduleExpressionTimezone, old Rule destroyed IN THE SAME CHANGE (no dual-trigger window), targeted plans, one product stack per wave; (P4) the NEVER#4(b) sweep -- every event-only pipeline gets a scheduled floor or a recorded exemption. PATTERN INSTANCE ALREADY EXECUTED: the cot 4:30 PM ET move (Andrew-direct ~0445Z 07-29; built @ce99054e44, plans cot 4/1/3 + mirror 4/0/3, applies post-17:15Z 07-29) and the etfs-reports-monthly-run precedent; the mdpf accrual bridge (cron(45 15)Z, deliberately UTC/chain-anchored) is the P2 counter-class instance.

hazards: A migration wave that ships the new Scheduler WITHOUT destroying the old Rule in the same apply creates a dual-trigger window -- double pulls, clobber class. The cot plans are the template: destroy rides the same targeted plan.

Do NOT migrate UTC-anchored-by-design triggers (chain-relative, e.g. the mdpf 15:45Z accrual bridge) to America/New_York for uniformity -- anchoring a chain-follower to a timezone its chain does not follow re-creates the drift class in the opposite direction. P2's ranking exists to prevent exactly this.

trigger-map.json freshness is load-bearing for every wave: a wave planned off a stale census migrates a trigger that no longer exists or misses one that does. The CI drift gate is the control; a wave plan cites the census vintage it was cut from.
